Subject: Examination & Format of EDLI Exemption/Extension Applications — reg

Reference : (i) Circular No. E-File No.27058 dated 29.04.2021.

(ii) Circular File No. f 8

(ii) Circular No. mption/2021/Extensi 2270) dt. 06.05.2022
Madam/Sir,

Kind attention is invited to Government of India notification GSR 299 (E) dated 28.04.2021
vide which Para 28(4) of the EDLI Scheme, 1976 was amended to include in addition to the Central
P.F. Commissioner, Addl. CPFC (Zone) as the authority to grant exemption to the establishments
where it is case of exemption of “class of employees” read with section 17(2B) of EPF & MP Act,
1952. A copy of the Notification was circulated by Head Office vide letter dated 29.4.2021 cited
at Sl. No. (i) above.

2 Vide circular dated 08.02.2022 and 06.05.2022, all the Addl. CPFC Zones were instructed
to re-examine the cases forwarded to Head Office as to whether they were eligible for grant of
exemption under Section 17(2A) or Section 17 (2B) bringing out the basic difference in the nature
of grant of exemption. Off late very few proposals have been forwarded to Head Office under
Section 17(2A) but after scrutiny it has been found that even they do not qualify to be considered
under Section 17(2A). There is a huge backlog of such applications and matter needs urgent
attention of all concerned. In this regard it is observed that most of the establishments that submit
proposal for grant of exemption from the EDLI Scheme, seek exemption only for their regular /
direct employees who are on their rolls and for whom the ECR is being filed by the establishment.
Contractual employees or employees engaged through Contractor/s, daily wage workers, etc. are
not included in the exemption applications. As all employees of the establishments are not included,
such applications come under “class of employees” and not for an establishment as a whole.

3. It is reiterated that in the cases falling under section 17(2A) for which the authority is the
Central PF Commissioner, the Addl. CPFC, Zone has to enclose a certificate that the exemption has
to be granted under section 17(2A) and the establishment shall comply/is complying in respect of

“de

all the categories and classes of employees including contractual and casual ones in its own EPF
Code number. In case the exemption is sought only for regular employees (or any other class of
employees), it is to be treated as exemption for class of employees for which Zonal Addl. CPFCs
are competent authority under Section 17(2B) read with Para 28(4) of EDLI Scheme,1976.

4. In addition to the above clarification the following procedure shall be followed by the Addl.
CPFC (Zones) and RPFCs in-charge of the ROs for processing applications for grant of exemption
or extension of exemption under Section 17(2A) of the Act:-

i) The applications complete in all respects will be scrutinized by RPFCs in-charge before
forwarding to the Addl. CPFC (Zone) and stating clearly the section under which approval of grant
of exemption is required.

ii) The requisite documents such as Group Insurance Policy, acceptance of the policy by majority
of the employees, advance premium receipts, benefit comparison statement, declaration of the
employer for coverage of all categories of employees and EOs report shall be enclosed.

iii) Addl. CPFCs (Zones) will scrutinize the exemption applications carefully and determine whether

the request pertains to the whole of the establishment [Section 17(2A)] or a class of employees
[Section 17(2B)] as clarified above. The Addl. CPFCs Zones shall grant exemption to all such
applications which fall under section 17(2B) either retrospectively or prospectively by exercising
the powers under section 17(2B) read with para 28(4) of EDLI Scheme, 1952. The proposal shall
be forwarded for grant of exemption/extension of exemption in the prescribed proforma and
Certificate only if the case falls under section 17(2A).

iv) Where it has been certified that the the case falls under section 17(2A), the Addl. CPFC (Zone)
will forward the proposal in the prescribed proforma with the requisite certificates to Head Office
(Format enclosed in Annexure-A and B). Physical applications, and other documents need
not be forwarded to Head Office.

5. It is also reiterated that proper classification of the establishments is also important to be
undertaken simultaneously as already instructed by Head Office in the last review meetings held
with all the Zonal Offices and completed in a time bound manner which is being monitored by
Head Office also. This is also a priority area consequent to the implementation of the Revised ECR
which has come effect for the wage month of September 2025. ACCs(Zones) may ensure that all
pending applications for EDLI exemptions may be processed and disposed by November 30th 2025.

(This issues with the approval of the Central PF Commissioner)
